statement: The function returns a result r such that len(r) = len(arr) and: (a) if there are indices 0 <= i < j < len(arr) with arr[i] > arr[j], then r is the lexicographically largest vector s with len(s)=len(arr) such that s is obtainable from arr by swapping two distinct positions and s <_lex arr; (b) if no such pair of indices exists (equivalently arr[0] <= arr[1] <= ... <= arr[len(arr)-1]), then r = arr. Here s <_lex arr means there is an index k with 0 <= k < len(arr) such that s[t]=arr[t] for every t with 0 <= t < k and s[k] < arr[k]. A vector s is obtainable from arr by swapping two distinct positions if there exist p and q with 0 <= p < q < len(arr) such that s[p]=arr[q], s[q]=arr[p], and s[t]=arr[t] for every t with 0 <= t < len(arr) and t not in {p,q}.
